facts.fact: FIJ reports that NIMC lists NIN verification clients including banks, data processing agencies and telecommunication services.
FIJ reports that NIMC lists banks, data processing agencies and telecommunication services as NIN verification clients.

NGA.note: No link between civil register and ID stated.

facts.fact: FIJ cites the Cybercrimes Act, sections 6 and 22, as the law in force against unauthorised access to systems and identity theft.

NGA.note: No arrest or prosecution under the Act is stated.

facts.fact: FIJ cites the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 as making unauthorised processing of personal data unlawful, with fines up to N10 million or 1% of gross annual revenue.

NGA.note: No decision or sanction under the Act is stated.

facts.fact: FIJ cites the NIMC Act 2007, section 14, as allowing only NIMC and its licensed agents to register individuals or offer NIN services, with offences in sections 18 and 30.
FIJ cites NIMC's 2017 Regulations on Registration of Persons and Licensing of Agents as allowing only authorised vendors to operate enrolment systems or connect to NIMC infrastructure.

NGA.note: No count or share of people holding a NIN.
Nothing on who operates or maintains the platform.
No public register keyed on the NIN stated.

facts.fact: FIJ describes NIMC as running NIN enrolment through licensed front-end partners, with a National Identity Database and NIN printing and verification services.
